chunks: As for what Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from Aḥmad ibn al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī, from al-Ḥakam ibn Miskīn, from Muʿāwiyah ibn Shurayḥ, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: When the Imam breaks wudu (ablution) while he is in the salat (prayer), it is not fitting that anyone step forward except one who witnessed the iqāmah.

Thus, the proper understanding of this report is that it indicates a kind of recommendation. For that reason, he said, “it is not fitting,” and did not say, “it is not permissible,” and that is explicit in indicating reprehensibility.

key_terms.أَحْدَثَ: invalidated ritual purity by an occurrence requiring wudu (ablution)
key_terms.الِاسْتِحْبَابِ: recommendedness; an act being preferable but not obligatory
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: the call immediately preceding the commencement of congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader in congregational salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْكَرَاهِيَةِ: reprehensibility; something discouraged without being forbidden
key_terms.يَتَقَدَّمَ: to step forward and assume leadership in the prayer

ai.seo_question: If the Imam breaks wudu (ablution) during congregational salat (prayer), who should step forward to lead?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for congregational salat (prayer) when the Imam invalidates his wudu (ablution) during the prayer. It indicates that the one who steps forward to complete the prayer should preferably be someone who witnessed the iqāmah, and the wording shows this is a matter of recommendation and karāhah rather than prohibition.
